name: Lip lift (bullhorn / subnasal)
lead: A lip lift is a surgical procedure that shortens the vertical distance between the base of the nose and the upper lip by removing a strip of skin, raising the lip and showing more of the vermilion, the pink part of the lip. In the subnasal or "bullhorn" version the incision is hidden under the nose [1][2].

Early descriptions in plastic surgery journals appeared in the early 1980s, presenting the operation as a correction of the lengthened upper lip seen with aging and thin lips [3][4][5]. A 1986 paper reported results in 83 patients, with scars hidden under the nose [6]. Later reports include a 28-year series of direct excision approaches to the aging mouth [7].
In looksmaxxing communities the lip lift is discussed as a "hardmaxx" option for a long philtrum, with posters linking it to ideas such as chin-to-philtrum ratio and midface proportions.[8]

paras: The procedure excises a shaped strip of skin, often a wavy or gull-wing ellipse, along the junction of the nose and lip, then closes it so the lip is raised. The goal is to shorten the philtrum and increase the amount of upper vermilion shown [1][2]. Variants place the incision along the vermilion border instead [3][4].

Grokipedia, an AI-generated reference, gives typical philtrum lengths of about 12-15 mm for women and 15-17 mm for men as targets and credits an earlier 1971 description to Cardoso and Sperli [2]. These figures come from an unverified source.

A 1981 British Journal of Plastic Surgery paper titled "Lip lifting" and a 1984 Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery paper on correction of thin lips described the operation [9][4]. The 1984 article described lifting and everting the lips along the vermilion border in 32 cases [4]. In 1986 the technique with the scar hidden under the nose was reported in 83 patients [3]. A 1992 article and a 2009 report of 28 years of experience continued the line of work on the aging mouth [10][7].

Evidence consists of surgeon case series. The 1986 report described minimal scars and excellent results in 83 patients [3]. The 1984 report on thin lips described a vermilion-border approach in 32 patients [4]. A 2009 paper reported 28 years of experience with direct excision for the aging mouth [7]. Facial feminization surgery reviews list lip shortening among procedures offered to some transgender women [11]. A registered trial in the source list tests an energy device for lifting the upper lip, which is a nonsurgical comparison [12]. No randomized trial of the surgical lip lift was found.

The main limitation discussed in the literature is scarring, which authors try to hide under the nose or along the lip border [3]. Posters on looksmax.org also describe swelling, noticeable early scarring and an excessive tooth or gum show after surgery, though these are personal accounts [8][13].

One forum poster reported a philtrum shortened from about 2 cm to 1.5 cm, said it improved eye spacing appearance, chin-to-philtrum ratio and lip thickness, and described heavy swelling for several days and a cost of about 450-500 USD abroad [8]. Other threads ask whether the surgery can be done at 15, with replies suggesting waiting until adulthood, or ask whether fillers or fat grafting would suit better [13]. Scarless and non-incision variants are also discussed [14].

lore.intro: Lip lifts are discussed on looksmax.org as a way to fix a long philtrum.[8]

claims.claim: Shortening the philtrum by a few millimetres improves several ratios at once.
claims.believers: A poster listed better midface ratio, facial width-to-height ratio, chin-to-philtrum ratio and a fuller-looking lip after removing 5 mm.[8]
claims.experts: Surgical literature describes shortening a long upper lip and increasing vermilion show; measurements of the claimed ratio changes are not reported in the abstracts reviewed.[3][4]

claims.believers: The poster said a cosmetic cream concealed the scar.[8]
claims.experts: Papers describe placing the incision beneath the nose or along the border to hide scars, with minimal scars reported in a case series.[3]

claims.claim: Many people who want a lip lift need filler or fat grafting instead.
claims.believers: A forum reply said roughly half of those asking might need fat grafts or filler.[13]
claims.experts: Fillers add volume but do not shorten the philtrum, per Grokipedia.[2]

card.summary: Surgery that shortens a long philtrum by removing skin under the nose; permanent, with the scar as the main trade-off.
card.aka: Bullhorn lip lift, subnasal lip lift, philtrum shortening
card.note: Permanent surgery; evidence is surgeon case series.

quick.overview:
A lip lift removes a strip of skin between the nose and upper lip so the lip sits higher and more pink shows. The bullhorn version hides the scar under the nose.

Published support is surgeon case series from the 1980s onward. Forum users discuss it for long philtrums.
quick.mechanism: Skin excision shortens the philtrum and raises the vermilion. Variants differ in where the incision is placed.
quick.risks: Surgery is permanent. Scarring is the main concern in the literature; forum accounts mention swelling and uncertain results.
